statement: Three different numbers are chosen at random from $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$. What is the probability that their sum is even?

choices.misconception: I thought the sum is even only when all three numbers have the same parity, so I counted 4 all-even plus 10 all-odd out of 84.
I counted the 40 choices with exactly two odd numbers but forgot the 4 choices with no odd numbers at all.
I assumed even and odd sums are equally likely, but there are more odd numbers than even numbers in the set.
I thought three odd numbers add to an even number, so I added the 10 all-odd choices to the correct 44.

hints: Only the number of odd numbers chosen matters.
A sum is even exactly when it contains an even number of odd terms. Count the selections with zero odd numbers and with two odd numbers, using the 5 odd and 4 even numbers.
No odds: $\binom{4}{3} = 4$. Two odds: $\binom{5}{2}\binom{4}{1} = 40$. Total selections: $\binom{9}{3} = 84$.

solutions.reliable: There are $\binom{9}{3} = 84$ equally likely choices. The set has $5$ odd numbers and $4$ even numbers, and the sum is even exactly when the number of odd numbers chosen is $0$ or $2$. Zero odd: $\binom{4}{3} = 4$. Two odd and one even: $\binom{5}{2} \cdot 4 = 40$. So the probability is $44/84 = 11/21$. Check with the complement: one odd, $5 \cdot \binom{4}{2} = 30$; three odd, $\binom{5}{3} = 10$; $30 + 10 = 40$ and $44 + 40 = 84$. Transferable idea: for a parity question, sort the objects by parity and count by how many odd ones you take.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
